private_note: I can't know or even estimate which fifth I'm in, and the plan lasts a generation with no revision, so I'm guarding against the worst case. Hazel gives the highest floor (41), then Birch (36), then Alder (32). Today's floor is 22 and Cedar's is 15, so I'd rather the convention fail than adopt Cedar. If Hazel stalls I'll move to Alder, since it beats Today in the bottom groups and costs the top very little.
statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows where we will land, and we can't even estimate the odds. Whatever we pick, we live under it for a generation. So I ask one question of each plan: if I turn out to be in the lowest fifth, how do I live? Hazel gives the lowest group 41 thousand, the most any plan can sustain. It's nearly double today's 22, and the middle still gets 64. Cedar drops the bottom to 15 with no health coverage, and every one of us might be standing there. I'll never vote for it. I rank Hazel first, then Birch, then Alder. To those who fear losing a top-fifth income: you might just as well be at the bottom, and Hazel's top still gets 159. We need nine votes, and if we fail we keep today's 22. I hope we can rally around Hazel. I'm also open to Alder if that's where agreement lies.
